title: Implement exact-before-fallback polling
evidence_required: FT-001-AC-001 — RED_NOT_APPLICABLE: because the baseline already sends no higher-price ad when an exact match exists, and manufacturing claim absence would break preserved behavior; alternative proof: record pre-implementation GREEN from mixed exact/fallback candidates for both successful and failed exact delivery. GREEN: the claim-equivalent post-change scenarios identify the exact match before delivery and capture zero fallback sends for both delivery outcomes, with the failed exact ID still unseen. Decisive comparison: exact-match presence implies fallback-send count = 0 in captured Telegram requests before and after the change, while temporary-SQLite state distinguishes confirmed from failed delivery. Artifact: .tasks/TASK-001-T2-FT-001-W1/TASK-001-T2-FT-001-W1-acceptance-evidence.md.

FT-001-AC-002 — RED: with PriceMax=1000, a completed exact-empty baseline poll containing otherwise eligible prices 1001, 1200 (first), 1200 (second), and 1500 sends zero fallback ads instead of the required closest three. GREEN: the same poll captures prices [1001, 1200(first), 1200(second)] in that order, excludes the fourth candidate and prices above 1500 or unknown, and a separate PriceMax-absent poll shows no fallback pass, fallback-only request, or duplicate delivery. Decisive comparison: captured Somon detail order and Telegram output differ from baseline zero fallback to the expected ordered three only when PriceMax is present; the absent-PriceMax trace contains no fallback phase. Artifact: .tasks/TASK-001-T2-FT-001-W1/TASK-001-T2-FT-001-W1-acceptance-evidence.md.

FT-001-AC-003 — RED_NOT_APPLICABLE: because baseline seen-ID exclusion, final-rejection seen writes, and no-result silence already satisfy this claim; alternative proof: record pre-implementation GREEN from captured transport and temporary-SQLite post-state. GREEN: claim-equivalent post-change scenarios make pre-seen IDs trigger no detail or delivery request, make unknown-price, over-ceiling, and other final rejections silent and seen, and capture zero ad messages when no eligible fresh candidate exists. Decisive comparison: requested/delivered ID sets and the SQLite seen set equal the expected per-ID classification before and after the change. Artifact: .tasks/TASK-001-T2-FT-001-W1/TASK-001-T2-FT-001-W1-acceptance-evidence.md.

FT-001-AC-004 — RED: with an exact-empty poll, remaining detail capacity, and an eligible higher-price candidate, the baseline performs no fallback delivery and prematurely treats the candidate as rejected, so shared-cap fallback lifecycle is absent; preserve separate pre-implementation GREEN observations for existing cap, 403/429 backoff, and delivery-retry behavior. GREEN: claim-equivalent low-cap and typed-failure scenarios show one counter shared by exact and fallback details, cap exhaustion or unresolved exact detail suppressing fallback and leaving deferred IDs unseen, 403/429 retaining backoff, failed exact/fallback delivery remaining unseen, and a complete exact-empty poll with spare capacity delivering fallback. Decisive comparison: per-scenario detail-request count never exceeds MaxDetailsPerPoll, fallback-send count matches completeness, and temporary-SQLite state distinguishes final rejection from deferred, blocked, transient, and failed-delivery IDs. Artifact: .tasks/TASK-001-T2-FT-001-W1/TASK-001-T2-FT-001-W1-acceptance-evidence.md.

FT-001-AC-005 / REQ-006 — RED_NOT_APPLICABLE: because the baseline already has no forbidden mechanism and adding one merely to observe RED would falsify the claim; alternative proof: record pre-implementation GREEN from the production-source/dependency inventory and native build. GREEN: post-change repository diff and owner review show no new schema, setting, dependency, worker, compatibility layer, second history model, or duplicate candidate/state-transition owner, and ./scripts/build.sh passes. Decisive comparison: pre/post go.mod, go.sum, storage/config surfaces, changed production paths, and boundary ownership show only reuse of Settings.PriceMax, seen_ads, the scheduler, existing clients/cap, Polling Application orchestration, and pure Filtering support. Artifact: .tasks/TASK-001-T2-FT-001-W1/TASK-001-T2-FT-001-W1-acceptance-evidence.md.
purpose: Provide useful closest higher-price alternatives only after a conclusively exact-empty poll while preserving existing freshness, cap, backoff, and delivery safety.
success_outcome: One active poll sends exact matches with priority or, only after complete exact-empty evaluation, sends at most three eligible fresh higher-price ads in deterministic order; all cap, error, delivery, and seen transitions match FT-001 without new durable machinery.
anti_goals: Do not add or reinterpret SQLite schema or persisted settings.
Do not add dependencies, workers, compatibility layers, configurable fallback controls, or separate shown history.
Do not move candidate orchestration or seen-state decisions into Somon, Telegram, Filtering, Persistence, Shared Data, or composition owners.
Do not implement FT-002 Telegram administration or FT-003 production release behavior.

stop_conditions: A required change cannot stay inside the accepted Polling Application and pure Filtering ownership/contracts.
Execution requires a schema, persisted setting, dependency, worker, compatibility layer, or separate history model.
Execution reveals an unresolved product behavior, public contract, data authority, or task-boundary decision.
Execution triggers T3 or cannot obtain honest claim-linked RED/GREEN evidence in the existing isolated test harness.

constraints: Keep one Go modular monolith and the accepted package dependency graph.
Use Settings.PriceMax only; derive floor(1.5 * PriceMax) in memory and send no fallback without PriceMax.
Keep proof, tests, RED/GREEN, and UAT with this implementation task.
Use the existing httptest Somon/Telegram and temporary-SQLite harness; no live or production probe is required.
Expected paths are advisory and non-exhaustive; any additional file must remain necessary to this same outcome and respect ownership.
invariants: Exact evaluation precedes fallback; an exact match or incomplete exact evaluation suppresses fallback.
Exact and fallback detail requests share MaxDetailsPerPoll.
Only IDs fresh at poll start are eligible; final rejection and confirmed delivery become seen, while deferred, transient, blocked, and failed-delivery outcomes remain unseen as specified.
Fallback requires known PriceMax < price <= floor(1.5 * PriceMax), every other filter, ascending price with stable feed-order ties, and a maximum of three sends.
Polling Application alone orders candidate phases and requests seen transitions; Filtering remains pure and adapters retain their existing boundaries.
No schema, setting, dependency, worker, compatibility layer, second history model, or duplicate candidate/state-transition owner is added.
verification_targets: FT-001-AC-001: app integration scenarios with mixed exact/fallback cards and Telegram success/failure prove that any exact match suppresses fallback.

FT-001-AC-002: deterministic app integration scenarios prove that absent PriceMax causes no fallback pass or fallback-only delivery and that present PriceMax enforces open lower/inclusive upper bounds, ascending price, stable feed-order ties, and exclusion after the third fallback candidate.
FT-001-AC-003: temporary-SQLite post-state and captured Telegram calls prove seen-ID exclusion, final-rejection seen writes, ineligible silence, and no-output exact-empty behavior.
FT-001-AC-004: low-cap and typed Somon/Telegram failure scenarios prove shared-cap suppression, backoff preservation, and unseen retry semantics.

FT-001-AC-005 / REQ-006: repository diff and owner review plus ./scripts/build.sh prove no new schema, setting, dependency, worker, compatibility layer, second history model, or duplicate candidate/state-transition owner while preserving the native build gate.
